checks: The hinge remainder is supported on the shrinking slab of width |εv_j| and bounded in absolute value by |εv_j|. Common domination bounds its integral uniformly by B times the reference slab mass, which tends to zero by the exact cut-null premise.
The linear term is continuous on the weakly compact feasible family by Portmanteau, because every weak limit in that family gives zero mass to the cutting planes.

A maximizer at the old threshold with largest linear term gives the lower bound. Compactness gives a cluster law of displaced maximizers, and the Lipschitz control plus continuity put it among the old maximizers. Testing the same law at the old threshold then gives the reverse bound.
The unrestricted derivative requires local equality of values, which the last sentence obtains from convex-order repair for nonnegative hinge coefficients only.
